name: TypeScript Strict Mode
description: Enforces strict TypeScript patterns — no any, explicit return types, null checks
content:
# TypeScript Strict Mode Rules

- Never use `any` type — use `unknown` and narrow with type guards
- Always provide explicit return types for exported functions
- Use strict null checks — no implicit null/undefined
- Prefer `interface` over `type` for object shapes
- Use `readonly` for properties that shouldn't be mutated
- Avoid type assertions (`as`) — use type guards instead
